title: The session was authorized on the server, so the endpoint being controlled was never asked whether the file may be written and run
index_line: T-0087 · EXEC · client-side file transfer/execution accepted on session authority alone, no Host confirmation · dotnet · corroborated
invariant_violated: Authorization was decided where the session was created — a role holding TransferFiles rights, checked by the server — and the endpoint that actually receives and runs the file was left out of the decision. The host's own consent was assumed to be implied by the session's existence, so a permitted session could write and execute on a machine whose user never agreed.

mechanism.does: file-transfer and file-execution actions arrive at the host client over an already-open remote session
the action is authorized only against the server-side role (TransferFiles) that the technician holds
the client accepts the transfer instruction and resolves the destination on the host, including elevated-execution actions
the transferred file is written into the host's writable location
the client launches the transferred file as part of the same action
attacker-supplied code runs on the host with the client's (often elevated) privileges, without the host user ever approving it

source.protocol.value: the remote-session control channel: file-transfer/file-execute actions multiplexed with the technician's session

guard.none.value: no host-side consent or authorization check for receiving and executing a transferred file — the server's role check is the only gate

sink.file.write.value: the transferred file landing on the host's filesystem

sink.exec.shell.value: the client executing the transferred file, including elevated execution actions

preconditions.expr: a role holds the TransferFiles permission for the session group in use

check.spec: printf 'enumerate roles via admin UI: Admin > Security > Roles > <role> > session group permissions > TransferFiles\n'

preconditions.expr: file-transfer actions complete on the host without prompting the host user

check.spec: printf 'observe host for RunFiles/RanFiles audit entries attributed to Process: Guest during a test transfer\n'

success: a file appears on the host and is executed without any host-side prompt
session audit records a file-transfer/execute action with no corresponding user approval on the endpoint
failure_like: the client refuses the transfer without explicit host consent (26.6.5+)
the role lacks TransferFiles, so the server rejects the action before it reaches the client
false_positive: a technician transferring files with the host user watching and approving is the intended workflow, not this bug — require execution with no host confirmation
a file-transfer entry alone is not proof; the execution of the transferred file is

hazards: every remote-support/RMM agent: the endpoint is a deputy that can write and run on behalf of whoever holds a session
the pattern is 'authorization decided at the control plane, action executed on the data plane with no local check'
worm-shaped propagation: a compromised endpoint can push the same payload to endpoints it later connects to
non_transfers: clients that require a per-action host prompt or a pre-approved policy on the endpoint

evidence.target: ConnectWise ScreenConnect client before 26.6.5, file-transfer/file-execution in active sessions (CVE-2026-84869)

provenance.author: ConnectWise (bulletin 2026-09-08)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-84869: a condition in the ScreenConnect client may allow files to be transferred and executed through an active remote session without authorization or Host confirmation; classified Missing Authorization; the 26.6.5 patch strengthens client and session handling for file-transfer and file-execution actions, and the interim mitigation is to remove the TransferFiles permission from roles

provenance.author: Huntress Labs
provenance.corroborates: independent analysis of the campaign exploiting it: earlier versions had a client-side flaw in file-transfer handling where transfer actions could proceed during an active session without proper authorization or confirmation from the Host, enabling files to be transferred to and executed on the Host, including elevated execution actions; RunFiles/RanFiles audit entries from Process: Guest

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-84869 description (file transfer/execution without authorization or Host confirmation), CVSS 9.9
